inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD flows, NZD rate. Build-up: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5% + beta ~0.9 x ERP ~5.75% = cost of equity ~9.7%; pre-tax debt ~6.0% (retail bonds 5.8-6.75%), 4.3% after 28% tax; debt ~21% of EV at the market price -> ~8.6%. The base 9.0% is the prior version's rate, deliberately UNCHANGED (it sits ~0.4pt above the build-up). What changed is that all three scenarios now use the same 9.0%: the prior version ran bull at 8% and bear at 11% on top of scenario flows that already carry the customer-concentration, contract-renewal and demand-decline risk, which charges that risk twice (owner-fcf-adaptations 7f). Evidence that would move the rate: a material shift in the NZ 10-year yield, or leverage leaving the 3.0-4.5x target band. This is the single most sensitive input - see the sensitivity grid and required_return_table.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial - lease liabilities $0.8m, lease interest $21k (FY2025). Left inside reported EBITDA and excluded from net debt; no lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: None - no non-controlling interests. The 25% Somerton pipeline interest is a joint operation whose revenue and costs are already inside reported revenue and EBITDA, so there is no bridge item for it.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, three scenarios (make build-dcf). Routed as an operating company (dcf-methods routing table): a single-site contracted fuel terminal and pipeline with its own EBITDA, capex and debt - not a REIT, trust or lender, so unlevered flows at WACC less net debt is the right frame. Same model as the prior version (legacy hand-built JSON dated 2026-08-10); this is the first build through the Drivers route. FY0 = FY2025 (last full statements); year 1 = FY2026, anchored to the August 2026 guidance. Only the H1-2026 results presentation was available (no interim statements), so H1 cash flow, tax and share data are from slides. Pre-2022 history is the closed refinery and is not used. Company 'Normalised FCF' ($66.9m FY2025) excludes growth, conversion and site-redevelopment capex; last_fcf here is statutory owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC), which the prior version did not use (it carried 67.6). Interest income ($0.12m) is not stripped: the company is in net debt. House and street bases coincide to within ~1c (SBC ~0.2% of revenue). Not valued: Marsden Point Energy Precinct / biorefinery optionality beyond the bull case's faster-growth path.
inputs.share_count_basis: ESTIMATE, flagged. 412,198,231 shares on issue at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 AR, contributed equity note) plus Dividend Reinvestment Plan issues for the March 2026 final dividend (~1.9m shares, assuming the ~20% uptake seen in Sept 2025) and the Sept 2026 interim dividend (~1.9m shares at the disclosed 20.3% uptake) = ~416.0m. Only the H1-2026 results presentation was available, not the interim statements, so the exact count should be replaced from the next filing; each 1m shares is ~0.3c per share. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and DRP shares are issued at market for cash that stays in the business, so they are value-neutral rather than dilution to be modelled.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt $365m is the Q3 2026 operational update figure (30 Sep 2026), the latest disclosed; $346m at 30 Jun 2026 (HY2026 presentation) and $329.9m at 31 Dec 2025. total_debt/cash split (368/3) is indicative - only the net figure was disclosed after year-end. Company definition: bank debt + retail bonds less cash, excluding the CHI030 fair-value movement. Lease liabilities ($0.8m) are immaterial.
inputs.da_note: da_pct_path is TAX depreciation, not the accounting charge. The FY2024 revaluation lifted book depreciation to ~$44-45m a year (31% of revenue), but depreciation on a revaluation uplift is not deductible. The FY2025 deferred-tax note shows the PP&E deferred tax liability unwinding by $5.2m, i.e. book depreciation exceeded tax depreciation by ~$18m, putting tax depreciation near $26m (~18% of revenue). The path starts there, holds ~17-17.5% while the 2026-2028 growth capex is being depreciated, and converges toward the maintenance capex rate by year 10 so the terminal year does not capitalise a tax shield larger than the capex that sustains it.
inputs.capex_note: capex_pct_path = maintenance capex at 9% of revenue (guidance 8-10%; FY2025 8.8%) PLUS the committed non-maintenance capex still to be spent after the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet date, because the revenue it buys is credited in growth_rates. Base build ($m): FY2026 ~14 maintenance + ~20 for Q4 (bitumen terminal completion, bp tank repurposing start, bund conversion, site redevelopment); FY2027 ~15.5 + bp ~40 + conversion ~18 + storage extension ~10 + site ~3; FY2028 ~15.5 + bp ~19 + extension ~8 + site ~2; FY2029-30 extension tail; 9% thereafter. Sources: HY2026 presentation contract table (bp $65-70m over 2026-2028, conversion ~$27m remaining across H2 2026 and 2027, storage extension $20-26m across FY26-FY30). Growth capex spent before 30 Sep 2026 is already in net debt and is not charged again.

equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR note 5: unused tax losses $374m (DTA $104.7m at 28%). Flows are taxed at a full 28% on EBIT from year 1, so the shelter is valued once here and never perpetuated. Assumed used against taxable income (EBITDA - tax depreciation - interest - provision spend) of ~57/62/63/72/78/42m over FY2026-FY2031; tax saved 16.0/17.4/17.6/20.2/21.8/11.8m discounted at 9%. At risk if the 49% shareholder-continuity test is breached.

equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR provisions note: $79.3m at 31 Dec 2025, less the HY2026 $7.2m jetty-restoration reassessment and ~$3m eliminated by the CCR Platformer sale = ~$69m, x (1 - 28%) because the spend is deductible. A discounted legacy-refinery obligation whose cash cost is not in the terminal's operating flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: bottom-up contracted revenue build (average of the base 10-year path); not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: STRUCTURAL BREAK: the refinery closed in 2022 and the site became an import terminal, so FY2018-FY2021 describe a different business and every 3- and 5-year CAGR spans the break - left null deliberately. Equity CAGR is not usable either: FY2024 equity rose on a $381m revaluation and a $50m raise while retained earnings stay deeply negative. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC) went -26.7 -> 12.1 -> 24.0 over FY2023-FY2025 as conversion capex ran down, which is not a growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is ~0.2% of revenue, so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF series are effectively the same.

base.narrative: Contracts as signed, one judgment call on the diesel reserve. FY2026 lands mid-guidance (EBITDA ~$105.5m on ~$156.5m revenue). FY2027 gets the full-year Z Energy jet storage, Higgins bitumen and Government diesel contributions plus PPI. FY2028 is flat: the Government diesel contract ends December 2027 (assumed re-let at ~60% of the fee), the TSA fixed fee steps down from $40m to $35m pre-PPI in April 2028, offset by the bp storage contract starting Q3 2028 and indexation. FY2029 takes the bp full year; thereafter PPI-like 2.2-2.6% with throughput flat.

bull.narrative: FY2026 at the top of guidance; the diesel reserve is renewed in full as the 28-day stockholding obligation bites from July 2028; further storage deals follow the bp template and precinct tenants (biorefinery FID in 2027) start paying for land and infrastructure. Margin climbs to ~71.5% on operating leverage. The extra revenue is not free: capex stays above maintenance until FY2033, at roughly the capital intensity of the bp contract.

bear.narrative: FY2026 at the bottom of guidance. The Government diesel contract lapses at end-2027 and the tanks sit idle, the fixed-fee step-down lands, and high fuel prices plus EV uptake pull variable throughput fees down faster than PPI lifts them, so revenue falls ~7% in FY2028 and is flat from FY2030. Costs keep inflating against a flat top line (margin drifts to 62.5%), maintenance capex runs at 10% on ageing assets, and the terminal multiple is capped at 11x for a declining-volume asset facing the 2032 TSA renewal.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25, unchanged from the prior version. Bear is above the 15% house default because ~95% of revenue comes from three customers, the largest new revenue line (Government diesel, ~8% of FY2027 revenue) expires in 13 months with no renewal announced, and leverage is rising toward the top half of the 3.0-4.5x band. Bull is below the 35% default because it needs several independent things - diesel renewal, further storage deals and a biorefinery FID that has already slipped twice. Base at 50%: it is mostly signed contracts.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Channel is a contracted, PPI-linked infrastructure income asset - the only pipeline to Auckland and NZ's only fuel import terminal - not a growth compounder. The model values the signed contracts, charges the capex that delivers them, taxes the flows at a full 28% with the NZ$374m of tax losses valued separately, and deducts the legacy demolition provisions. On that basis every scenario sits below the market price: the weighted value implies about 9x FY2026 EBITDA against roughly 16x in the market. The gap is discount rate and optionality rather than a disagreement about near-term earnings, which the model takes straight from guidance.
valuation_philosophy.changes_from_prior: Three corrections to the prior (2026-08-10) method, each explained in the reconciliation bridge: (1) growth, conversion and site capex are now charged - the prior version credited contracted growth while charging maintenance capex only; (2) the tax shield uses tax depreciation (~17% of revenue), not revaluation-inflated book depreciation (~30%); (3) one WACC across scenarios. Two additions to the bridge: the tax losses (+) and the demolition/restoration provisions (-).
deliberately_unchanged: Base WACC 9.0% - moves on a material change in NZ long bond yields or leverage leaving the 3.0-4.5x band.
Terminal growth 2.0 / 2.5 / 1.0% and terminal caps 16x / 20x / 11x - move on an updated Envisory throughput outlook or the terms of the 2032 TSA renewal.

Maintenance capex 9% of revenue (10% bear) - moves if guidance leaves 8-10% or the three-yearly asset revaluation signals shorter asset lives. HY2026 ran 11.7% on phasing; management reaffirmed the full-year range.
Cash tax rate 28% from year 1 - statutory; the loss shelter is in the equity bridge instead.
SBC 0.2% of revenue; weights 25/50/25; base growth for years 8-10 (2.6/2.4/2.2%); bull growth years 5-10; bear growth years 5-10.
changed_drivers: Growth years 1-4 in all scenarios: August 2026 guidance upgrade ($103-108m EBITDA), the FY2027 contribution disclosure (~$9m + ~$14m), the December 2027 diesel contract expiry, the April 2028 fixed-fee step-down and the bp contract from Q3 2028. Base years 5-7 trimmed from 3.5/3.0/2.8% to 2.6% because the contract phase-in those years stood for is now modelled explicitly in years 1-4.

EBITDA margin: year 1 from guidance; base matures at 68.2% rather than 68.8% after the fixed-fee step-down. Bull and bear margin paths are new - the legacy file held only a terminal FCF margin for them.
Capex, D&A, WACC (bull/bear), working-capital capture (5% -> 0: a terminal operator billing monthly in arrears has no prepaid float to collect on growth).
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: the valuation is terminal-heavy and long-duration; see the sensitivity grid. At 7% the base value is ~2.0 with the 16x terminal cap binding, so no cell of the grid reaches the market price - the price needs both a lower required return and a richer exit multiple, or uncontracted precinct income.
Government diesel storage renewal after December 2027 - worth roughly $13m of near-pure-margin revenue either way.
Tax depreciation is inferred from the deferred-tax note, not disclosed; if the true figure is nearer book depreciation the value is ~25c higher.
Share count and the debt/cash split are estimates pending the interim statements.
2032 Terminal Services Agreement renewal terms; customer concentration (bp, Mobil, Z Energy ~95% of revenue).
Tax losses depend on the 49% shareholder-continuity test.
Unvalued upside: biorefinery / Energy Precinct land income beyond the bull path.
